thread_a.role: ICMP send rate-limit check (lockless fast path)

thread_b.role: concurrent ICMP send refill/update (same function, self-race)

emergent_bug.violated_requirement: ρ = atomic([read(icmp_global.credit)]) from thread_a (the lockless fast-path empty-bucket read must not interleave with a conflicting write)
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@icmp_global_allow:272 = mutate(icmp_global.credit = credit) on another CPU
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: thread_b writes credit/stamp while holding icmp_global.lock, but thread_a reads credit (and stamp) on the fast path BEFORE acquiring icmp_global.lock; a one-sided lock does not serialize the lockless fast-path read → no g establishes atomic(read)
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ρ is atomic over a single access (an unmarked lockless read concurrent with a conflicting write) → data race / load-store tearing

fix_maps_to: READ_ONCE() on the fast-path reads of icmp_global.credit/stamp paired with WRITE_ONCE() on the locked writes of icmp_global.stamp/credit → marks the accesses as single-copy-atomic (establishes atomic(read/write) at the C-memory-model level); the lock is unchanged
recall_risk_notes: Clean one-sided-lock self-race in a single file on a static global (easy to enumerate and ground; surface pre-fills icmp_global.credit/stamp + icmp_global.lock candidate). Risk: the lockless read is a DELIBERATE fast-path optimization (source comment: check empty bucket 'without taking the spinlock'), so an LLM may judge it intentional/benign and decline to assert atomic(read), suppressing the report; it is also a benign rate-limiter tearing race.
